title: Arrows between finite sums of affine etale free module sheaves descend
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed preorder, $D:I^{op}\to\mathrm{Scheme}$ an inverse system of qcqs schemes with affine transitions, and $(X,\pi)$ a limit cone [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. For an etale object $W$ of $X$, let $P(W)$ be the sheafification of $V\mapsto\Lambda[\mathrm{Hom}(V,W)]$ [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module], [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Given finite families of affine etale objects $U_1,\ldots,U_n$ and $V_1,\ldots,V_m$ and an arbitrary arrow $f:\bigoplus_jP(V_j)\to\bigoplus_kP(U_k)$, there exist $i\in I$, constructible module sheaves $A,B$ on $D_i$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], an arrow $a:A\to B$, and isomorphisms $e_A:\pi_i^{-1}A\cong\bigoplus_jP(V_j)$ and $e_B:\pi_i^{-1}B\cong\bigoplus_kP(U_k)$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], such that $e_B\circ\pi_i^{-1}a=f\circ e_A$.

source.place: Tag 09YU (3), fully faithful and essentially surjective arguments using 095N; parent split steps 3-6 and the constructibility of A,B in step 7. Verified at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09YU and /tag/095N.

proof.text: Descend the finite affine etale families U and V to a common stage, as in step 3 of the parent node. Choose a common upper bound; base change each object to it. The resulting free-sheaf isomorphisms transport the original arrow f.

source.place: Lemma 09YU, proof of (1), paragraph 'Essentially surjective' (lines 12607-12619): 'U is the base change of a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme etale over X_i for some i ... Limits, Lemmas 01ZM and 07RP'

proof.text: Let Q be the sum of free sheaves on the descended U objects. Free-sheaf inverse image and preservation of coproducts give eB from the inverse image of Q to the original target. Represent the arrow out of each V free summand by its generating section, using the free-Yoneda and sheafification adjunctions. The ModuleCat-valued form of this compatibility can also be constructed directly from Etale.upperStarLowerStarAdjunction: the free sheaf represents sections, and lowerStar evaluates on the base-changed object. Co-Yoneda gives the free-sheaf comparison and naturality gives its section compatibility.

source.place: Lemma 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change), lines 11492-11514; the module case of 09YU, whose details Stacks omits (line 12625)

proof.text: Apply the section-colimit theorem to Q and each descended V object. Represent the finitely many generating sections at finitely many stages, choose a common upper bound, and transport sections there using the theorem's compatibility. Let A be the sum of the free V sheaves there and let B be the pullback of Q to this common stage.

source.place: Lemma 09YU, proof of (1), paragraphs 'Fully faithful' (lines 12589-12605) and 'Essentially surjective' (lines 12607-12619); Theorem 09YQ (theorem-colimit), lines 7400-7411

proof.text: The descended sections define a : A -> B by the free-Yoneda bijection and coproduct universal property. Base change of the free summands gives eA and composition gives eB. To show L.map a followed by eB.hom equals eA.hom followed by f, precompose with each free coprojection and evaluate on its identity generator. The unit-section compatibility and the defining section comparison give equality of these generating sections; free Yoneda and the coproduct universal property give the claimed square.

source.place: Lemma 09YU, proof of (1), paragraph 'Fully faithful' (lines 12589-12605), adapted to sheaves of modules as Stacks instructs for (3) (lines 12621-12625; details omitted there)

proof.text: The free sheaf on an affine etale object is the etale lower shriek of the constant coefficient module: both represent sections by their adjunctions. It is constructible by the etale-free-sheaf theorem. Using the comparison of the two constructibility predicates, apply the source library's closure under finite sums and its pullback theorem. Thus A and B are constructible. The empty family gives the zero sheaf, also constructible.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_affine_free_etaleModule_arrow_descent
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty I]
    (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u})
    [∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map f)]
    [∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, CompactSpace (D.obj i)]
    [∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i)]
    (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c)
    (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] [Finite Λ]
    (n m : ℕ) (U : Fin n → c.pt.Etale) (V : Fin m → c.pt.Etale)
    (hU : ∀ k : Fin n, IsAffine (U k).left)
    (hV : ∀ k : Fin m, IsAffine (V k).left) :
    let P : c.pt.Etale → Sheaf c.pt.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) :=
      fun W => (presheafToSheaf c.pt.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)).obj
        (uliftYoneda.{u + 1}.obj W ⋙ ModuleCat.free Λ)
    ∀ f : (∐ fun j : Fin m => P (V j)) ⟶ (∐ fun k : Fin n => P (U k)),
      ∃ (i : I)
        (A B : Sheaf (D.obj (op i)).smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))
        (a : A ⟶ B),
        IsConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf A ∧ IsConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf B ∧
        ∃ (eA : (Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) (c.π.app (op i))).obj A ≅
            (∐ fun j : Fin m => P (V j)))
          (eB : (Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) (c.π.app (op i))).obj B ≅
            (∐ fun k : Fin n => P (U k))),
          (Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) (c.π.app (op i))).map a ≫ eB.hom =
            eA.hom ≫ f
